author: Frosty
text:
Hi Aran, Its very nice to meet you, brother

I'm a noob in this forum and still absorbing a lot of materials in. I'm
being guided by bro Staurum through these pages of market truth and
still in the 'I'm lost and stuck' category of people regarding RTM
materials, but from looking at your trades and your trade calls such as
the one from your post (please see below), I definitely will not lose
faith in this method

As for the chart above, I don't know what is blocking me to see why the
part that you marked "I would watch PA here for buy opportunity" is a
good place for a buy? What I understood until now is that it is a DP to
break the high that I marked with a red line and it is also an FTR after
 the break of the green line, which is a local high and is, to my
knowledge (can be wrong), less significant.

I can't seem to understand why the box that has your marking is the best
 place to buy, rather than the FTR after the break of the blue line that
 I drew in the purple box. Would you please explain or give some hints
about this, brother? The biggest confusion for me as of now is the
reason why sometimes price reacts to the DP to engulf and other times
price reacts to the important FTR (which we call FL). I don't know what
to look for on the charts regarding this matter and hours of screentime,
 imho, will be pretty much wasted if I don't know what I should be
looking for in the first place

Also, I'm just curious about your trading journey. At the start of your
trading journey, i.e. when you first tried your RTM style trades, did
you have a tight SL at the start or did the SL placement improves and
gets better and tighter with more knowledge and screentime? I think I
might have warped expectations regarding entries and SL at this early
stage of my learning that our SL should be as tight as the masters' SL,
which is close to zero drawdown
 I'm looking to hear your view on this brother because as of now, I seem
 to be looking only for "to-the-pip" bounces from the materials taught
here in RTM. Am I going about learning this in the wrong way? or should I
 start with defining larger zones to trade at first and then working on
to narrow these zones with practice?

Thank you in advance brother Please forgive any comments/wordings that might sound offensive (I'm not a native english speaker )
 I appreciate any comments from you regarding the two questions above if
 you don't mind me asking. Please keep on posting trades and trade ideas
 so I can learn more from you, brother

author: AranJibril
text:
Hey Frosty, Welcome and very nice to meet you too brother,

Firstly sorry to confuse you, you are definitely right about the purple
box, i was only aware of it after i posted it, and regarding your
question about SL placement well at first i wasn't using SL then after i
 got burned a couple of times then started to use them, but it was wide
generally and then started to get tighter with time, IMHO i think it's
better to focus on learning each concept in RTM individually then with
chart time connecting it to read the market and know the direction that
price will go to next correctly then after that focus on tight SL,
because it will be overwhelming at the beginning if you try to do it all
 at once and will bring you unnecessary stress that may delay your
progress, you are doing good already just keep that pace

author: HCDE
text:
Hi Frosty

I think you should do like me, forget tight stoploss at the beginning,
it will just bring you the frustration of being stopped out everytime.

My opinion is that as long as you don't master the way a FLAG is
considered complete, you won't be able to see the real edges of it so
it's dangerous fo you, and i'm telling you that but that's my main
problem too

I saw Aran Jibril journal a long time yesterday and to my opinion he
even goes beyond that, sometimes he put his stoploss not beyond the FLAG
 but beyond the last valid DP of the FL and it makes the SL very very
tight, it seems a little bit riskier to me but with time and experience
on price action maybe you can manage it correctly.

About your question on FTR and DP, that's very interesting question and i'm struggling too with that.

As far as i understand, FTR and DP are the same thing, it's just a
matter of scale. A DP, on smaller scale, is a FTR. And they start the
construction of FLAG on the ground of lower timeframe FTR (ie, DP). Does
 it means that every DP will be the base for a FLAG? No, we have to
watch price action... But they can be important. And if you think about
it from IT point of view, it's logical. This LTF DP are often in the
middle of nowhere, where no one will think to buy or to seel so it's
good time for them to do this or that...

author: Frosty
text:
@ Aran,

Thank you for the response brother, now I am a little bit relieved to
see that people other than the masters didn't have a razor thin SL at
first tries. I've always thought that we should strive for those types
of super tight SL otherwise there should be no trade I really should stop imagining and assuming things and ask them directly from more experienced traders like you.

Also thank you for clearing that question about the FTR, brother. I'm
relieved that I got that right so at least some of my analysis is not
off the mark. From the updated chart that you post, it seems that your
box seems to be the best place for the bounce, but that was the FTR
(your blue box) of an FTR (purple box, which I believe is the FL). Any
hints on why price bounced off from your blue box instead of the purple
FTR (the FO zone)? This is the main confusion for me as of now and I'm
quite lost as there seems to be no clear explanations on them.

Sorry to ask you a lot of questions, brother. Thank you in advance for
your kind reply. Looking forward to see more trades from you, brother

@ HCDE

I was thinking of the same thing actually about the SL. A few of my
analysis that I stored in my personal notes actually got a decent bounce
 to the wider zone, but not the exact, to-the-pip, level. I will follow
your advice, brother. I'm actually still reading up on FLs and trying to
 complete the QM homework explanations first before touching FLs, as bro
 Staurum said that I need to master FTRs and PAZs first.

The question on FTR/FL and DP, what I can't seem to find the answer is
there any clues that we can see on the chart before the actual FO to DP
actually occurs? The only thing that I can think of that ITs can do is
to place fake SRs, e.g. double tops or bottoms, and FO to the DP before
going into their desired direction. But in some trades (I'll try to find
 some posts later) that I read, expert RTMers seem to have figured out
where they should place their orders in the FO zone (the DP) and not the
 FTR/FL.

I have read somewhere from bro Staurum's post compiled from other
members that gives an explanation of this, but I lost the link somewhere
 in my hard drive
 I'll post it again in my journal for reference and for further
discussion when I find it, brother. Thank you for your explanations
brother, it really helps me to understand more tricks that the IT can
play

Again, thank you both for your kind reply

your risk appetite on which one you use, price sometimes react to FTR of
 the FL and some other times to the FL it self, off course FL is as far
as it can get, provided the analysis is correct, so SL should be behind
that FL, Hope this answers your question
